recognize_zh: Steiner 銀染色使背景呈黃棕色，壞死區內可見少數細小的深色短桿狀或顆粒狀構造，可能對應 Bartonella henselae 桿菌；但此圖解析度與對焦有限，菌體難以明確辨認，須在高倍油鏡下確認成簇的彎曲桿菌。
features: Silver (Steiner) stain with yellow-brown background of granular necrotic debris
Rare tiny dark short rod-like and punctate particles within the necrotic material
No definite clusters or chains of pleomorphic bacilli resolvable at this focus and magnification
Occasional larger dark brown granules, likely pigment or debris
describe_en: Steiner silver stain of the necrotic area shows a yellow-brown background of granular debris with rare tiny dark rod-like and punctate particles. Definite clusters or chains of pleomorphic bacilli are not convincingly resolved at this magnification and focus, and nonspecific silver deposition on debris cannot be excluded. In cat scratch disease, Bartonella henselae appears as small black, pleomorphic, curved bacilli in clusters, often in necrotic areas and vessel walls, best evaluated under oil immersion; a negative or equivocal silver stain does not exclude the diagnosis, and serology or PCR is more sensitive.

ddx.vs: Precipitate is irregular in size and distributed in the background and extracellularly rather than forming uniform, clustered small bacilli.
Mycobacteria stain poorly with silver impregnation and are identified with acid-fast stains.
Treponema appear as long, thin, tightly coiled spirochetes rather than short pleomorphic bacilli.
